title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Hearing Civil Dispute Cases Involving Infringement of the Right of Information Network Dissemination
keywords_en: tort liability; copyright; civil dispute over infringement of the right of communication through information networks
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court of the People's Republic of China

Announcement

The Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Infringement of the Right to Communicate Works through Information Networks were adopted at the 1561st session of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on November 26, 2012, and are hereby promulgated for implementation as of January 1, 2013.

December 17, 2012

Supreme People's Court

Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Infringement of the Right to Communicate Works through Information Networks

Interpretation No. 20 [2012]

For the purpose of correctly trying civil disputes over infringement of the right to communicate works through information networks, protecting the right to communicate works through information networks in accordance with the law, promoting the healthy development of the information network industry, and safeguarding the public interest, these Provisions are formulated in accordance with the relevant legal provisions such as the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, the Tort Law of the People's Republic of China, the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and in light of the actual circumstances of trial.

Article 1 When trying civil disputes over infringement of the right to communicate works through information networks, the people's courts shall, in the exercise of their discretion in accordance with the law, take into account the interests of the right holder, the network service provider, and the public.

Article 2 The term "information network" as used in these Provisions includes computer internet, broadcast television networks, fixed communication networks, mobile communication networks and other information networks with electronic devices such as computers, televisions, fixed telephones, and mobile phones as terminals, as well as local area networks open to the public.

Article 3 Where a network user or network service provider, without permission, provides through an information network a work, performance, or sound recording or video recording over which a right holder has the right to communicate through information networks, the people's court shall, unless otherwise provided by laws or administrative regulations, determine that the act constitutes an infringement of the right to communicate through information networks.

Where a work, performance, or sound recording or video recording is placed in an information network by means of uploading to a network server, setting up shared files, or using file-sharing software, enabling the public to obtain it by downloading, browsing or other means at a time and place individually selected by them, the people's court shall determine that the act of making available as provided in the preceding paragraph has been carried out.

Article 4 Where there is evidence proving that a network service provider and another person jointly provide works, performances, or sound recordings or video recordings through division of labor or other cooperation, thus constituting joint infringement, the people's court shall order them to bear joint and several liability. Where a network service provider can prove that it only provides network services such as automatic access, automatic transmission, information storage space, search, links, or file-sharing technology, the people's court shall support its claim that it does not constitute joint infringement.

Article 5 Where a network service provider substantially replaces the provision of relevant works to the public by other network service providers by means such as providing web page snapshots or thumbnails, the people's court shall determine that it constitutes an act of making available.

Where the act of making available as provided in the preceding paragraph does not affect the normal use of the relevant work and does not unreasonably harm the legitimate rights and interests of the right holder in that work, the people's court shall support the network service provider's claim that it has not infringed the right to communicate works through information networks.

Article 6 Where the plaintiff has prima facie evidence that a network service provider has provided relevant works, performances, or sound recordings or video recordings, but the network service provider can prove that it only provided network services and is not at fault, the people's court shall not determine that it has committed infringement.

Article 7 Where a network service provider induces or assists a network user in committing an act of infringement of the right to communicate works through information networks when providing network services, the people's court shall order it to bear tort liability.

Where a network service provider induces or encourages a network user to commit an act of infringement of the right to communicate works through information networks by means such as words, promoting technical support, or offering bonus points, the people's court shall determine that it constitutes an act of inducing infringement.

Where a network service provider knew or should have known that a network user was infringing the right to communicate works through information networks by using network services, and fails to take necessary measures such as deletion, blocking, or disconnection of links, or provides assistance such as technical support, the people's court shall determine that it constitutes an act of assisting infringement.

Article 8 The people's court shall determine whether a network service provider bears liability for inducing or assisting infringement based on its fault. The fault of a network service provider includes actual knowledge or constructive knowledge of the network user's infringement of the right to communicate works through information networks.

The people's court shall not determine that a network service provider is at fault solely because it fails to proactively examine acts of network users infringing the right to communicate works through information networks.

Where a network service provider can prove that it has taken reasonable and effective technical measures but still finds it difficult to discover a network user's infringement of the right to communicate works through information networks, the people's court shall determine that it is not at fault.

Article 9 The people's court shall, based on whether the specific facts of a network user's infringement of the right to communicate works through information networks are obvious, comprehensively consider the following factors to determine whether a network service provider constitutes constructive knowledge:

(1) The ability to manage information that should be possessed based on the nature and manner of the network service provided and the likelihood of inducing infringement;

(2) The type and popularity of the works, performances, or sound recordings or video recordings disseminated and the obviousness of the infringing information;

(3) Whether the network service provider has proactively selected, edited, modified, or recommended the works, performances, or sound recordings or video recordings;

(4) Whether the network service provider has actively taken reasonable measures to prevent infringement;

(5) Whether the network service provider has set up convenient procedures for receiving infringement notices and has responded reasonably to infringement notices in a timely manner;

(6) Whether the network service provider has taken corresponding reasonable measures against repeated infringement by the same network user;

(7) Other relevant factors.

Article 10 Where a network service provider, when providing network services, recommends popular film and television works or the like by setting up rankings, catalogs, indexes, descriptive paragraphs, content introductions, or other means, and the public can directly obtain them by downloading, browsing, or other means on its webpage, the people's court may determine that it should have known that the network user was infringing the right to communicate works through information networks.

Article 11 Where a network service provider directly obtains economic benefits from works, performances, or sound recordings or video recordings provided by network users, the people's court shall determine that it bears a higher duty of care regarding the network user's infringement of the right to communicate works through information networks.

Where a network service provider places advertisements targeting specific works, performances, or sound recordings or video recordings and obtains revenue, or obtains economic benefits that have other specific connections with the works, performances, or sound recordings or video recordings it disseminates, it shall be deemed as directly obtaining economic benefits as provided in the preceding paragraph. The receipt by a network service provider of general advertising fees, service fees, or the like for providing network services does not fall within the circumstances provided in this paragraph.

Article 12 Under any of the following circumstances, the people's court may, based on the specific circumstances of the case, determine that a network service provider providing information storage space services should have known that a network user was infringing the right to communicate works through information networks:

(1) Placing popular film and television works or the like on the homepage or other main pages that can be clearly perceived by the network service provider;

(2) Proactively selecting, editing, organizing, or recommending the themes or content of popular film and television works or the like, or setting up dedicated rankings for them;

(3) Other circumstances where it can be clearly perceived that relevant works, performances, or sound recordings or video recordings are provided without permission, and reasonable measures are still not taken.

Article 13 Where a network service provider receives a notice submitted by a right holder by means of letter, fax, email, or other means but fails to timely take necessary measures such as deletion, blocking, or disconnection of links, the people's court shall determine that it had actual knowledge of the relevant infringement of the right to communicate works through information networks.

Article 14 In determining whether the necessary measures taken by a network service provider, such as deletion, blocking, or disconnection of links, are timely, the people's court shall make a comprehensive judgment based on factors such as the form of the notice submitted by the right holder, the accuracy of the notice, the difficulty of taking measures, the nature of the network service, and the type, popularity, and quantity of the works, performances, or sound recordings or video recordings involved.

Article 15 Civil disputes over infringement of the right to communicate works through information networks shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the infringing act occurred or where the defendant is domiciled. The place where the infringing act occurred includes the location of equipment such as network servers or computer terminals where the alleged infringing act was carried out. Where both the place where the infringing act occurred and the place where the defendant is domiciled are difficult to determine or are located outside the territory of the People's Republic of China, the location of equipment such as computer terminals where the plaintiff discovers the content of the infringement may be deemed as the place where the infringing act occurred.

Article 16 As of the date of implementation of these Provisions, the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Copyright in Computer Networks (Interpretation No. 11 [2006]) shall be simultaneously abolished.

Civil disputes over infringement of the right to communicate works through information networks that have not been finally adjudicated after the implementation of these Provisions shall be governed by these Provisions. For cases that have been finally adjudicated before the implementation of these Provisions, where the parties apply for retrial or a retrial is decided in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, these Provisions shall not apply.
